what: The 4B lane's finding applied to the 9B: the R224 32-row FP16 linear chunk re-reads the 2 GB vocabulary projection (248320 x 4096) once per piece; R293 pads or splits every unquantized-linear call into one verified oneDNN M-class per weight shape. Image qwen38-int4-fp16-linear-classpad-cheapest-r293 sha256:40d46730, VLLM_XPU_FP16_LINEAR_CLASSPAD=1, verified in every container. Chain script scripts/run-20260911-qwen35-9b-classpad-chain.sh, wrapper qwen35-9b-classpad-20260911.

server_census.248320x4096: classes 1-32 / 33-128 / 129-320 / 321-512, canonical 129-320 (most populous eligible; large weight)

s1_tp1_ladders.identity: MTP0 exact at every rung but c32 (127/128), 256/256 at c64; depth 3 exact through c16 except c12 (47/48), then 5-10% from c20 (R224 x1, two passes: MTP0 exact to c64, depth 3 exact to c16, 3-5% at c32/c64)
s1_tp1_ladders.reading: Same shape as the 4B. Depth 3 +26% at c16, +48% at c32, +56% at c64; no-speculation +29% at c64. Single user -3.2% (depth 3) and -3.6% (MTP0), smaller than the 4B's 5-6% because the 9B's per-layer projections are a smaller fraction of its step. Under R224 the depth-3 column was flat from c16 (747, 827, 787); under R293 it rises to 1228 and depth 3 leads no-speculation to about c32.
